title: Quarterly private deployment: acceptance criteria, rollout constraints, and measurable signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create a single, measurable quarterly plan that defines clear acceptance criteria, rollout constraints, and the observable signals we will use to declare success for Private/VPC/On‑Prem enterprise deployments. This ticket consolidates cross-functional decisions needed to translate initiative-level OKRs into testable gates and telemetry checks for the release window.
acceptance_criteria: Documented acceptance criteria for canary, staged, and GA waves (operational, performance, and security checks)
End-to-end runbook for rollback and customer communications validated in a dry-run with SRE and Support
Automated gating rules created in Console (traffic thresholds, error budgets, latency percentiles) with dashboards linked
Three representative enterprise customers on the pilot whitelist with signed test plans and success signoffs
Compatibility matrix covering KMS integrations, SSO flows, and network topology validated by Infra Engineering
explicit_constraints: No GA rollouts during calendar blackout windows for existing enterprise migrations (see infra calendar)
Max concurrent onprem upgrade slots = 6 per week unless capacity approved by Dedicated capacity team
All onprem installation artifacts must pass offline installer checksum validation and HSM integration tests
Feature flags in control plane must support per-customer gating and rapid rollback within 10 minutes
measurable_signals: Latency P95 for inference tail < 450ms for 95% of pilot tenants
Error budget burn rate < 5% per week during canary
Token unit cost delta within forecasted +/- 12% for dedicated/private variants
Audit log completeness: >99.9% of control plane events within 30s of occurrence
Successful end-to-end SSO login and KMS envelope decrypt tests for 100% of pilot accounts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Network egress restrictions prevent telemetry from reaching Console. Mitigation: Build an offline telemetry relay that can ship logs post-upgrade and validate metrics locally.
Risk: Third-party KMS vendors require additional certs. Mitigation: Pre-flight KMS compatibility checklist and escrowed test keys for pilot tenants.
Risk: Inference latency regression when customers enable quantization. Mitigation: Provide pre-configured quantization profiles and perf validation harness per customer.
Risk: Limited ops headcount for parallel upgrades. Mitigation: Staggered waves + runbook automation (self-service scripts) and on-call rotation augmentation.
decisions: Decision: Use staged waves (pilot -> canary -> broad) with a minimum 2-week observation window between phases
Decision: Require an automated rollback artifact per customer that can be triggered by Support within the Console
Decision: All pilot tenants must opt into telemetry sharing for the pilot period (legal signoff present)
rollout_phases: Phase 0 - Readiness (design docs, dry-run, infra capacity signoff)
Phase 1 - Pilot (3 enterprise tenants, feature-limited, 2-week window)
Phase 2 - Canary (10 tenants, gradual traffic ramp, strict SLO monitoring)
Phase 3 - Broad (GA, opt-in migrations, partner enablement)
open_questions: What is the allowed customer opt-out window for telemetry post-GA?
Do we require dedicated CCB approval for wave size > 20 customers?
Is there a minimum contract term for customers who request air-gapped installs?
next_steps: Schedule cross-functional kickoff (SRE, Security, Solutions Eng) by 2026-03-12
Finalize pilot tenant list and push test plans to GH by 2026-03-19
Create automated gating rules in Console and link dashboards by 2026-03-31
Run dry-run upgrade in staging with telemetry relay by 2026-04-05
